newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Energy Dept rejects bank's heating oil plan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Energy Dept rejects bank's heating oil plan.

text.p: The U.S. Energy Department turned down a proposal by Bankers Trust to arrange a deal involving oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to help cool heating oil prices, a department spokesman said Friday.

The plan, reviewed last week, was submitted on the heels of calls by Northeastern lawmakers and consumer advocates for the government to take steps to bolster heating oil supplies to avert a price shock this winter.
"It was determined by all that this particular plan could not deliver more heating oil into the market this winter," said Energy Department spokesman Bill Wicker.
"Additionally, there were associated risks to the government -- to the Treasury -- with no clear benefit to the public," he said.
He had no details on the plan, and Bankers Trust's energy group in Houston refused to comment on it.

While heating oil prices eased off five-year highs this week on industry and government reports that inventories had grown by 1.3 million barrels last week, Rep. Joe Kennedy, D-Massachusetts, said Friday the government should consider more market proposals.

"The continued low level of heating oil inventories demonstrates the need for the industry, working with the government, to take steps to build adequate supplies at reasonable prices," said Kennedy, who has advocated setting regional product reserves.
The Energy Department had received a string of proposals and "we look at each one of them carefully," Wicker said.
